599:
Located within the areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-25 where streams exist but no base flood data have been provided (A Zones), or where base flood data have been provided but a floodway has not been delineated, the following provisions apply:
(1) When base flood elevation data or floodway data have not been provided in accordance with section 16-25, then the mayor shall obtain, review, and reasonably utilize any scientific or historic base flood elevation and floodway data available from a federal, state, or other source, in order to administer the provisions of article II, division 3 of this chapter. Only if data are not available from these sources, then the following provisions in subsections (2) and (3) of this section shall apply.
(2) No encroachments, including structures or fill material, shall be located within an area equal to the width of the stream or 20 feet, whichever is greater, measured from the top of the stream bank, unless certification by a registered professional engineer is provided demonstrating that such encroachment shall not result in more than a one-foot increase in flood levels during the occurrence of the base flood discharge.
(3) Elevation.
a. In special flood hazard areas without base flood elevation data, new construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall have the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area (including basement) elevated no less than three feet above the highest adjacent grade at the building site. (Note: Require the lowest floor to be elevated one foot above the estimated base flood elevation in A Zone areas where a limited detail study has been completed). Openings sufficient to facilitate the unimpeded movements of floodwaters shall be provided in accordance with standards of section 16-82(4).
b. All heating and air conditioning equipment and components (including ductwork), all electrical, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities shall be elevated no less than three feet above the highest adjacent grade at the building site.
c. The mayor shall certify the lowest floor elevation level and the record shall become a permanent part of the permit file.
(Ord. of 8-12-2009, art. 4(C))
600:
Located within the areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-25 where streams with base flood elevations are provided but no floodways have been designated (Zones AE), the following provisions apply:
(1) No encroachments, including fill material, new structures or substantial improvements shall be located within areas of special flood hazard, unless certification by a registered professional engineer is provided demonstrating that the cumulative effect of the proposed development, when combined with all other existing and anticipated development, will not increase the water surface elevation of the base flood more than one foot at any point within the community. The engineering certification should be supported by technical data that conforms to standard hydraulic engineering principles.
(2) New construction or substantial improvements of buildings shall be elevated or floodproofed to elevations established in accordance with section 16-83.
(Ord. of 8-12-2009, art. 4(D))
601:
Areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-25 may include designated "AO" shallow flooding areas. These areas have base flood depths of one to three feet aboveground, with no clearly defined channel. The following provisions apply:
(1) All new construction and substantial improvements of residential and nonresidential structures shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to the flood depth number specified on the flood insurance rate map (FIRM), above the highest adjacent grade. If no flood depth number is specified, the lowest floor, including basement, shall be elevated at least three feet above the highest adjacent grade. Openings sufficient to facilitate the unimpeded movements of floodwaters shall be provided in accordance with standards of section 16-82(4). The mayor shall certify the lowest floor elevation level and the record shall become a permanent part of the permit file.
(2) New construction or the substantial improvement of a nonresidential structure may be floodproofed in lieu of elevation. The structure, together with attendant utility and sanitary facilities, must be designed to be watertight to the specified FIRM flood level plus one foot, above highest adjacent grade, with walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water, and structural components having the capability of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and the effect of buoyancy. A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted standards of practice for meeting the provisions above, and shall provide such certification to the official as set forth above and as required in section 16-52.
(3) Drainage paths shall be provided to guide floodwater around and away from any proposed structure.
(Ord. of 8-12-2009, art. 4(E))
602:
(a) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall be consistent with the need to minimize flood damage.
(b) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall have public utilities and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical and water systems located and constructed to minimize flood damage.
(c) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall have adequate drainage provided to reduce exposure to flood hazards.
(d) For subdivisions and/or developments greater than 50 lots or five acres, whichever is less, base flood elevation data shall be provided for subdivision and all other proposed development, including manufactured home parks and subdivisions. Any changes or revisions to the flood data adopted herein and shown on the FIRM shall be submitted to FEMA for review as a conditional letter of map revision (CLOMR) or conditional letter of map amendment (CLOMA), whichever is applicable. Upon completion of the project, the developer is responsible for submitting the as-built data to FEMA in order to obtain the final LOMR.
(Ord. of 8-12-2009, art. 4(F))
603:
(a) Critical facilities shall not be located in the 100-year floodplain or the 500-year floodplain.
(b) All ingress and egress from any critical facility must be protected to the 500-year flood elevation.
(Ord. of 8-12-2009, art. 4(G))

609:
This article shall be known, cited and referred to as the "Watkinsville Smoking Regulations." O.C.G.A. § 31-12A-12 (also see O.C.G.A. § 16-12-2, similar) provides:
"This article shall be cumulative to and shall not prohibit the enactment of any other general or local laws, rules, and regulations of state or local governing authorities or local ordinances prohibiting smoking which are more restrictive than this article or are not in direct conflict with this article."
Also see the federal Pro-Children's Act (Title X of Public Law 103-227), the Georgia Youth Access Law (O.C.G.A. § 16-12-171) and the No Child Left Behind Act.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-1))
610:
(a) The city council finds that:
(1) Studies have found that tobacco smoke is a major contributor to air pollution, and that breathing secondhand smoke is a cause of disease in healthy non-smokers, including heart disease, stroke, respiratory disease, and lung cancer.
(2) Tobacco use in the proximity of children and adults engaging in or watching recreational activities at city owned or operated facilities is detrimental to such children's and adults' health, and can be offensive to those using such facilities.
(3) Secondhand smoke is particularly hazardous to the elderly, people with cardiovascular disease, and individuals with impaired respiratory function, including asthmatics and those with obstructive disease. Children exposed to secondhand smoke have an increased risk of asthma, respiratory infections, sudden infant death syndrome, developmental abnormalities, and cancer.
(4) Cigarette butts are often discarded on the ground requiring maintenance expenses, diminish the beauty of the city's recreational facilities, and pose a risk to toddlers due to ingestion.
(5) The CDC warns that nicotine is highly addictive, and e-cigarettes may contain other harmful substances. Nicotine can harm adolescent brain development, and young people who use e-cigarettes may be more likely to smoke cigarettes in the future, according to the CDC.
(6) Atlanta, Alpharetta, Chamblee, Decatur, DeKalb County, Doraville, Douglasville, Duluth, Gainesville, Kennesaw, Marietta, Norcross, and Roswell voted to ban smoking in public parks.
(b) Accordingly, the city council finds and declares that the purposes of this article are:
(1) To protect the public health and welfare by prohibiting smoking in public parks;
(2) To guarantee the right of non-smokers to breathe smoke-free air; and
(3) To recognize that the need to breathe smoke-free air shall have priority over the desire to smoke.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-2))
611:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Smoking means vaping, including an e-cigarette; inhaling, exhaling, or carrying any lighted cigar, cigarette, pipe, weed, plant or other combustible substance in any manner or in any form.
Vaping includes "e-cigs," "e-hookahs," "mods," "vape pens," "vapes," "tank systems," and "electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS)."
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-3))
612:
(a) Unless otherwise provided, smoking is prohibited in all public park property in the city.
(b) Park property includes, but is not limited to, open areas, trails, buildings, lakes, ponds, streams, restrooms, athletic fields, playgrounds, off-leash areas, in vehicles, spectator and concession areas, streets, sidewalks and all other park areas.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-4))
613:
Smoking may occur no less than 50 feet outside any entrance to any place where smoking is prohibited.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-5))
614:
"No Smoking" signs or the international "No Smoking" symbol (consisting of a pictorial representations of a burning cigarette enclosed in a red circle with a red bar across it) shall be clearly and conspicuously posted at the entrance to every park where smoking is prohibited.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-8))
615:

(b) Any citizen who desires to register a complaint under this chapter may do so with the health department or the police department.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-9))
616:
No person shall retaliate against any person because such person exercises any right to a smoke-free environment.
(Ord. of 10-16-2019, exh. A(31-10))
617:

(1) A fine not exceeding $100.00 for a first violation;

618:

621:
This article shall be known, cited and referred to as the "Watkinsville Vaping Regulations." See the Federal Pro-Children's Act (Title X of Public Law 103-227), the Georgia Youth Access Law (O.C.G.A. tit. 16, ch. 12, art. 7 (O.C.G.A. § 16-12-171 et seq.)) and the No Child Left Behind Act.
(Ord. of 11-20-2019(3), exh. A(31A-1))
622:
(a) The city council finds:
(1) The Atlanta Journal Constitution and other news outlets have reported: "More than 500 people have been diagnosed with vaping-related breathing illnesses. An eighth death was reported this week," and "The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said 530 confirmed and probable cases have been reported in 38 states and one U.S. territory, up from 380 a week ago," and "Two-thirds of the cases involved 18- to 34-year-olds."
(2) Vaping is detrimental to one's health and can be offensive to those nearby.
(3) CNBC recently reported: "Senators Mitt Romney, R-Utah, and Jeff Merkley, D-Oregon, introduced a bill Thursday that would ban flavored e-cigarettes and apply cigarette taxes to the devices, among other measures aimed at curbing teen vaping. Called the Ending New Nicotine Dependencies (ENND) Act, the legislation would ban e-cigarette flavors other than tobacco, specify e-cigarette design standards, monitor the public health risks of using tobacco products, apply existing cigarette taxes to e-cigarettes and direct the Department of Health and Human Services to educate the public about health implications of using e-cigarettes. 'Vaping companies have hooked millions of our children on nicotine using e-cigarette flavors like "gummy bear," "Scooby snacks," and "strawberries and cream." This means massive health consequences for the next generation, and we have to end this addiction crisis,' Merkley said in a statement. 'We need to get these flavors off the market.'"
(4) The CDC warns that nicotine is highly addictive, and e-cigarettes may contain other harmful substances. Nicotine can harm adolescent brain development, and young people who use e-cigarettes may be more likely to smoke cigarettes in the future, according to the CDC.
(5) It was reported recently, in the context of the recent New York State ban on flavored e-cigarettes, that "...the New York State Department of Health [said]: 'nearly 40 percent of 12th grade students and 27 percent of high school students in New York State are now using e-cigarettes.' Additionally, in 2018, over a quarter of high schoolers (27.4 percent) were e-cigarette users, up 160 percent from 2014."
(b) Accordingly, city council finds and declares the purposes of this article are:
(1) To protect the public health and welfare by prohibiting sale of flavored vaping products;
(2) To protect the public health and welfare by prohibiting use or possession of flavored vaping products by those under the age of 21 years;
(3) To guarantee the right of non-vapers to breathe vapor-free air; and
(4) To recognize that the need to breathe vapor-free air shall have priority over the desire to vape.
(Ord. of 11-20-2019(3), exh. A(31A-2))
623:

624:

631:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— The Uniform Standards Code for Manufactured Homes Act, O.C.G.A. § 8-2-130 et seq.; ad valorem taxation of mobile homes, O.C.G.A. § 48-5-440 et seq.
635:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accessory use means a use customarily incidental to the principal use of the land.
Family means one or more persons occupying a dwelling and living as a single housekeeping unit, as distinguished from persons occupying a boardinghouse, lodginghouse, or hotel.
Lot means a parcel of land occupied or to be occupied by one or more main buildings and its accessory buildings with such open and parking spaces as are required by the provisions of this article and having its frontage upon a public street.
Mobile home means a movable or portable dwelling unit constructed to be towed on its own chassis, connected to utilities and designed without a permanent foundation for year-round occupancy, which can consist of one or more components that can be retracted for towing purposes and subsequently expanded for additional capacity, or two or more units separately towable but designed to be joined into one integral unit. Removal of wheels does not change the classification of the dwelling. Construction of a permanent foundation and other permanent improvements and attachments can change the classification of a mobile home to that of a modular building.
Mobile home park means any lot on which are customarily parked three or more mobile homes for a longer period of time than 30 days for rental purposes.
Modular building means a factory-fabricated, transportable building consisting of units designed to be incorporated at a building site on a permanent foundation into a permanent structure to be used for residential or commercial purposes. Placement of permanent foundation, porches, roof design and other like factors distinguish a modular building from a mobile home.
Open space means an area which is not used for or occupied by a driveway, off-street parking, loading space, yard or refuse storage space.
Plat means a map, plan or layout of a county, city, town, section, subdivision, or development indicating the location and boundaries of properties.
Principal use means the primary purpose for which land or a building is used.
Right-of-way line means the dividing line between a lot, tract or parcel of land and a contiguous right-of-way.
(Code 1982, § 36-201; Code 1994, § 24-26)
636:
When the provisions of this article impose more restrictive standards than are required in or under any statute or other legal document, the requirements of this article shall govern. When the provisions of any statute require more restrictive standards than are required by this article, the provisions of such statute shall govern.
(Code 1982, § 36-209; Code 1994, § 24-27)
637:
It shall be the duty of such appointed officer to enforce, interpret, and administer the provisions of this article.
(Code 1982, § 36-208; Code 1994, § 24-28)
638:
Any dwelling classified as a mobile home shall be required to be registered, and a building permit shall be obtained therefor from the city clerk.
(Code 1982, § 36-202; Code 1994, § 24-29)
639:
Mobile home parks must adhere to the following conditions:
(1) The minimum lot area per park shall be five acres. The minimum lot width for portion used for entrance and exit shall be 50 feet. The minimum lot width for portions containing mobile home spaces or stands shall be 50 feet.
(2) The minimum number of spaces completed and ready for occupancy before the first occupancy is permitted shall be 25 spaces, or 60 percent of developable area, excluding street and buffer, and the minimum area for each mobile home space or stand shall be 6,000 square feet.
(3) No space shall be rented for residential use of a mobile home in any such park except for periods of 30 days or more, and no mobile home shall be admitted to any park unless it can be demonstrated that it meets the requirements of any additional laws and regulations of the city council.
(4) In addition to meeting the requirements of this section, the mobile home park site plan shall be accompanied by a certificate of approval from the county health department.
(5) Paved drives at least 16 feet wide connecting to the interior drive shall be provided on each trailer site sufficient in length and width to serve as 1½ off-street parking space. In addition, paved driveways at least 16 feet wide shall also be provided to laundry buildings, other service buildings, and recreation buildings or areas.
(6) One refuse collection station shall be provided for each 20 families or fraction thereof, not more than 200 feet from any trailer served, and shall be conveniently located for collection. If individual refuse containers are used on the trailer site, these containers must be submerged in the ground with only the top portions extended above ground level. In lieu of a submerged unit, stands may be provided to hold the cans and screen them from conspicuous view.
(7) Each mobile home park shall be landscaped with shade trees and exterior screen planting.
(8) The owner of the mobile home park shall install a concrete patio at least four inches thick, with minimum dimensions of 15 feet by ten feet, within each trailer space.
(9) No mobile home shall be located within:
a. Ten feet of its individual lot line;
b. Twenty-five feet from any exterior boundary of the mobile home park.
(10) A buffer strip at least 25 feet wide shall be located adjacent to each exterior property line of the mobile home park and not be included within any individual trailer lot. This buffer strip shall be increased a width of 50 feet when located adjacent to property zoned for single-family residences. This strip shall be densely planted with fast growing evergreen shrubs or willow trees.
(Code 1982, § 36-203; Code 1994, § 24-30)
640:
In all districts where single mobile homes are allowed, they shall be subject to the following conditions:
(1) The lot area and dimensions must meet the requirements of the county health department in regard to water and sewer systems for individual mobile homes.
(2) In no case shall the unit be located within 200 feet of any permanent type of building, provided the owner of the building may waive in writing this requirement, but provided further that the distance shall be at least 50 feet.
(3) The mobile home unit must be supported under all exterior walls by a permanent foundation, completely enclosing the undercarriage, and must be connected to water and sewerage in compliance with the applicable requirements of the city council.
(4) A single unit mobile home must be equipped with tiedown bands and shall be anchored.
(5) All mobile homes used as residences shall be anchored.
(6) A single mobile home unit may be used for an office in a subdivision by the developer, temporary residence during construction of permanent residency, or for special purposes, for a period not to exceed six months upon written approval from the building inspector or the city council.
(7) Any single unit mobile home which does not meet the requirements of this section shall be removed after receipt of notice of its nonconformance from the building inspector or the city council.
(8) All mobile homes in the city must be served by a water and sewer system approved by the county health department.
(Code 1982, § 36-204; Code 1994, § 24-31)
641:
Any mobile home which is not anchored may blow over or off its blocks when the wind velocity reaches approximately 70 miles per hour. Therefore, this section is intended to make certain that all mobile homes hereafter placed in the city are equipped with tiedowns and are anchored.
(1) Tiedowns. All mobile homes placed in the city shall have tiedowns with provisions for distributing the load of these tiedowns, and provisions for the attachment to ground anchors so as to resist wind overturning and sliding. Each tiedown shall be designed to resist an allowable working load equal to or exceeding 3,150 pounds and shall be capable of withstanding a 50 percent overload without failure.
(2) Ground anchors. Ground anchors shall be installed at each mobile home stand when a mobile home is located thereon to permit tiedowns of mobile homes to comply with this section.
a. Each ground anchor shall be capable of resisting an allowable working load equal to or exceeding 3,150 pounds applied in the direction of the tiedown. In addition, each ground anchor shall be capable of withstanding a 50 percent overload without failure.
b. Ground anchors shall be resistant to weathering deterioration at least equivalent to that provided by a coating of zinc on steel strapping of not less than 0.30 ounces per square foot of surface coated.
(Code 1982, § 36-206; Code 1994, § 24-33)
642:
In every mobile home park, the following street improvements and utilities shall be planned for and provided by the developer, by installation or payment, prior to the approval of the mobile home park:
(1) All streets shall be named and marked with signs and shall include street grading and street paving.
a. Sanitary sewer lines or septic tanks shall be provided in conformity with requirements of the county health department.
b. All utilities except power lines shall be installed in the shoulders of the road underground.
(2) Base and paving shall consist of Type 1, 3½-inch compacted asphaltic concrete binder applied on top of a properly prepared subgrade which has been brought to a 95 percent compaction. A 1 1/2-inch hot plant mix type E topping shall be applied for the wearing surface or the equivalent of such paving and base.
(3) Mobile home park street pavement widths shall be 20 feet unless a street serves 15 homes or less. It may then be 18 feet wide.
(4) Linear street grades. Maximum and minimum linear street grades shall be as follows:
a. Collector streets, not more than 12 percent.
b. Subcollectors, lanes, and parking spaces, not more than 15 percent.
c. No linear street grade shall be less than one-half of one percent.
(5) Storm drainage facilities.
a. A registered engineer must certify that the proposed storm drainage improvements indicated on the mobile home park plan are adequate.
b. If a storm drainage sewer system exists in the city area, then the proposed mobile home park must contain an underground storm drainage system which shall be connected to the existing area system. Such system shall be indicated on the plat.
c. If a storm drainage sewer system does not exist in the city area, then adequate surface drainage facilities, as certified by an engineer, shall be included in the mobile home park and so indicated on the plan.
d. Where a proposed mobile home park is traversed by a watercourse, drainageway, channel, or stream, there shall be provided a stormwater easement or drainage right-of-way along each side of the channel or course for the purpose of widening, deepening, relocating, improving or protecting such drainage easement.
(6) Land for recreation and open space.
a. Any developer shall provide a minimum of 0.02 grassed acres of open space and recreation area per dwelling unit within the proposed mobile home park. In no case shall the amount of recreational land required be more than 20 percent. Any mobile home park which would be required to provide one-half acre or less in open space shall be absolved of this requirement. Not over 50 percent of this reserved area may be within a 100-year frequency flood area.
b. All property proposed for open space shall be:
1. Shown on the plan; and
2. Approved with respect to location and suitability.
(7) Zoning. Nothing in this section shall be construed to mean that land may be set aside for commercial purposes in a residential district, without the land so required for commercial uses being zoned appropriately or in accordance with zoning ordinances or regulations of the city.
(8) All mobile home subdivisions shall be required to meet all the standards and provisions of the subdivision regulations of the city.
(9) All mobile homes placed, erected, or located in the city shall be required to meet the adopted building, heating, plumbing, electrical, fire, gas, mechanical and air conditioning and all other codes adopted by the city.
(10) Community shelters. A common community shelter for severe winds shall be provided in the mobile home park.
(11) Penalties to single-family mobile homeowners. Failure by an owner of a mobile home to obtain and utilize tiedowns and anchors for such owner's mobile home placed in the city after the effective date of the regulations from which this article is derived shall constitute a misdemeanor.
(Code 1982, § 36-207; Code 1994, § 24-34)

645:
Said court shall be presided over by the judge of said court, and the judge and the judge(s) pro tem shall be licensed attorneys. No person shall be qualified or eligible to serve as judge unless such person is qualified to practice law in the Western Judicial Circuit.
(Code 1982, § 5-102; Code 1994, § 14-2; Ord. No. 2024.06.001, 6-19-2024)
646:
The bailiff of the municipal court shall be the police chief or designee. Duties of the bailiff shall consist generally of keeping order while the court is in session, and doing such other acts of assistance as may be required of such bailiff by the judge.
(Code 1982, § 5-103; Code 1994, § 14-3; Ord. No. 2024.06.001, 6-19-2024)
647:
The municipal court may fix punishment for offenses within its jurisdiction not exceeding a fine of $1,000.00 or imprisonment for 60 days, or both (no city work gang or on the streets, sidewalks, squares, or other public works). An appeal to the superior court shall be a de novo proceeding unless otherwise provided by law, including O.C.G.A. 5-3-1 et seq., the "Superior and State Court Appellate Practice Act." A record of all cases heard in the municipal court for violation of this Code or other municipal ordinances shall be kept in a suitable bound volume by the municipal court clerk. Such record shall contain the name of the defendant, the nature of the offense charged, the final disposition of the case, and the date of final disposition.
(Code 1982, § 5-104; Code 1994, § 14-4; Ord. No. 2024.06.001, 6-19-2024)
648:
Any person charged with violating any city ordinance shall receive notice by service of summons as provided in this section. Such summons may be issued by the municipal court clerk, the building inspector, or any police officer of the city. The summons shall be directed to the accused and shall distinctly state the offense charged, and the day, hour, and place of trial, requiring the accused to appear before the judge or the municipal court to answer the accusations made. Service of the summons shall be made by a police officer of the city either by serving the accused personally or by leaving a copy at the accused person's most notorious place of abode, except that in the case of a summons issued for violations of laws or ordinances relating to the parking of motor vehicles, such summons may be directed to an unknown person as owner of an automobile designated by the summons and may be served upon such person by leaving a copy in or attached to such automobile.
(Code 1982, § 5-105; Code 1994, § 14-5; Ord. No. 2024.06.001, 6-19-2024)
649:
The municipal court clerk shall issue subpoenas for the appearance of all witnesses necessary for the prosecution or for the defense in any case pending before the municipal court. All subpoenas shall be served in the same manner as a summons.
(Code 1982, § 5-106; Code 1994, § 14-6; Ord. No. 2024.06.001, 6-19-2024)
650:
Any person who fails to appear at the time and place set out in any summons or subpoena served upon such person shall be guilty of contempt of court and, upon conviction, shall be punished for such contempt of court.
(Code 1982, § 5-107; Code 1994, § 14-7)
651:
When a police officer or other authorized law enforcement officer or individual shall have effectuated a proper arrest upon any person for violation of any provision of this Code or any other applicable municipal ordinance or state or federal law, and a trial cannot be had immediately, the arresting officer or individual may allow the arrested person to post bond with good security therefor to ensure such arrested person's appearance before the municipal court or other appropriate court for disposition of said matter. The amount of said bond, the security therefor and the procedures in connection therewith shall in all respects be in conformity with, and the same as, the published procedures, amounts and qualifications as established from time to time by the county sheriff. 675:
(a) Findings. Law enforcement indicates that over time there has been an increase in juvenile crime; that persons under the age of 18 years are susceptible, by lack of maturity and experience, to participate in unlawful activity; that criminal activity from other areas appears to be infiltrating the county; and that there have been crimes such as substance abuse, entering autos, burglaries, damage to property, fighting, and other incidents.
(b) Intent. The city desires to protect minors, seeks enforcement of parental control over and responsibility for minors, strives for protection of the public, and implements this provision for reduction of criminal activities not easily controlled by existing laws and ordinances.
(c) Prohibited. It is a violation when a juvenile wanders or loiters about the streets of the city or in or about any highway or any public place between 12:00 midnight and 5:00 a.m.
(d) Police requests. The city council recognizes that in Mwangi v. State, 316 Ga. App. 52 (2012) the court held: "Even when officers have no basis for suspecting a particular individual, they may generally ask questions of that individual, ask to examine the individual's identification, and request consent to search, as long as police do not convey a message that compliance with their requests is required." The city council recognizes when an apparent juvenile declines to answer questions, provide identification or be searched, law enforcement sometimes needs additional tools to effectively police the community.
(e) Parental control. The council has determined a curfew for those under the age of 18 years will help attain the foregoing objectives and diminish the undesirable impact of such conduct, and promote the public good, safety and welfare. Parental responsibility for whereabouts of minors is the accepted norm, and legal sanctions to enforce such responsibility have demonstrated effectiveness in many cities. Law enforcement has reported the effectiveness of curfews in other counties such as Spalding, Clayton, Fayette, Cherokee, Chatham, Murray, Coffee, and Gwinnett. The city council has determined a curfew will increase parental responsibility for minors, decrease minor delinquency including criminal activity, and decrease truancy and tardiness.
(f) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Emergency errand means a mission from unforeseen circumstances that call for immediate action. Includes fire, natural disaster, auto accident, or any situation requiring immediate action to prevent serious bodily injury or loss of life.
Loiter. See section 24-56. Also see O.C.G.A. § 16-11-36.
Minor means a non-emancipated person under the age of 18 years.
Public place means any place to which the public has access.
Wander, as distinct from loitering (separately addressed below), means to move around without a definite purpose; to go or extend in an irregular course or direction; to ramble without a definite purpose; roam, rove, to go aimlessly, indirectly, or casually, moving or going about without plan or fixed destination or going to a destination by an indirect route, or in current vernacular, hanging out, or roaming the streets.
(g) Exceptions. It shall be unlawful between 12:00 midnight and 5:00 a.m. for any minor to loiter or to wander in any public place unsupervised by such minor's parent, legal guardian, or adult over 21 years of age having the lawful care and custody of the minor and having the lawful authority to be at such places; and provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply to the following:
(1) Minor on any emergency errand directed by such minor's parent, guardian, or adult of 21 years of age or older having the lawful care and custody of the minor;
(2) Minor returning directly home from a school activity;
(3) Minor traveling to, or returning directly home from, lawful employment that makes it necessary to be in above referenced placed during the proscribed period of time;
(4) Minor attending or traveling directly to or from an activity involving the exercise of First Amendment Rights of free speech, free assembly, or free exercise of religion;
(5) Minor engaged in vehicular travel through the city with parental consent;
(6) Minor is married or has been married pursuant to state law.
(h) Violation. It shall be unlawful for the parent, guardian, or other person having custody or control of any minor to permit or, by insufficient control, to allow such minor to violate the rules herein. A person in violation of this section for the first time shall be given a warning. Upon subsequent violation, the person shall be charged with such as a misdemeanor. Jurisdiction of juvenile and municipal courts. Any minor under 17 years of age shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the juvenile court. Any minor 17 years of age charged with violating this article shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the municipal court.

(c) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

The city shall record the expenses incurred in abating graffiti and shall provide a statement of such costs to the owner/occupant. If any expenses remain unpaid after 30 days, the city may sue to recover all expenses incurred by the city in removing the graffiti, including attorney fees and court costs associated therewith.

The court may suspend or probate a portion or its entire sentence upon such conditions to include the restoring of the property so defaced, damaged or destroyed, or other remedial action.

719:
(a) Based on the experiences of other counties and municipalities, relevant to the problems faced by the city, the city council notes the conditions and occurrences generally associated with adult entertainment establishments. The city council finds that adult entertainment establishments result in an increase in criminal behavior and create undesirable community conditions. An increase in disorderly conduct, public drunkenness, public indecency, public solicitation, violent crime, prostitution, exploitation of young women, drug use, drug trafficking, and loitering of individuals with criminal histories has been the experience of other counties and municipalities that permit adult entertainment. Conditions in other counties and municipalities are depression of property values in neighborhoods surrounding adult entertainment, community blight, an increased burden on and expenditure for law enforcement, and an increase in the criminal case load due to the crime problems.
(b) The city council recognizes that lawful adult entertainment implicates First Amendment protection, and it has no desire to censor or control protected speech. The city council has neither any animosity toward nude entertainment nor any desire to chill protected expression. The city council has narrowly tailored these regulations to combat the negative secondary effects and protect the public health, safety, and welfare and to allow reasonable avenues of protected First Amendment communication. (a) Title. This article shall be known and may be cited as the "Watkinsville Alarm Control Ordinance."
(b) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alarm contractor means whoever installs, maintains, repairs, alters, monitors or services alarm systems for compensation. An alarm contractor shall meet the requirements for an alarm system contractor pursuant to state statutes. Alarm contractors shall maintain a 24-hour emergency telephone number and shall be capable of responding to an emergency service call within four hours.
Alarm protocol means a systematic program, as determined by the police or fire department, to verify or otherwise confirm the validity of an alarm signal at a banking or other financial institution or any other business or service facility where deemed appropriate by the police or fire department.
Alarm system means any device designed to be used for detection of smoke or fire or of any unauthorized entry, or for alerting others of the possible commission of an unlawful act, or both, which emits a sound or transmits a signal and/or message when activated. Excluded from the definition of alarm systems are devices not designed or used to register alarms that are audible, visible or perceptible outside of the protected building, structure or facility; or auxiliary devices installed by municipal utilities or telephone companies to protect utility systems from damage or disruption of services; or audible alarms affixed to motor vehicles. If an alarm system is designed to activate an audible alarm, the alarm system shall automatically deactivate the audible alarm after no more than 30 minutes of operation.
Audible alarm means a device designed for the detection of fire or smoke or of unauthorized entry on premises which generates an audible sound when it is activated.
Commercial premises means a structure or area not defined herein as a residential premises.
False alarm means an alarm signal caused by other than an emergency situation, or which is not caused by the activation of either an alarm system or audible alarm as the result of fire or smoke, a burglary, robbery, assault, forced entry or attempted forced entry into the premises. An alarm will be deemed a false alarm when there is no substantial physical evidence which would clearly indicate that smoke, fire or a criminal act was the sole reason for activation of the alarm signal or when the alarm system was intentionally activated by an individual under circumstances where there was no articulable and reasonable basis to believe that a fire, crime or other emergency, had occurred or was occurring, or was about to occur. The failure to abide by the established, current, alarm protocol by those responsible on the premises will be considered a separate false alarm under this definition.
Notice means written notice, given either by mail or by personal service upon the addressee.
Residential premises means any structure or combination of structures which serve as dwelling units, including single-family as well as multifamily units.
(c) Posting of premises; deactivation of alarm system. If any such person shall fail to appear to turn off an alarm within 15 minutes after being notified by 911 Dispatch to do so, then this shall constitute a false alarm and the alarm contractor and owner or manager of the premises shall be in violation of and shall be punishable as misdemeanor.
(d) Required reports of false alarms; corrective actions; penalties.
(1) Responsibility for all false alarms shall be borne by the person or persons occupying or controlling the premises. For each response by the police or fire department to any false alarm, the person owning or maintaining such alarm system shall submit such reports as are set forth herein, or be in violation, as follows:
a. For any two responses recorded by the police or fire department during any calendar year period to a premises where a false alarm has occurred, no violation hereof shall exist; however, the person having or maintaining the burglary or fire alarm or the alarm protocol shall, within ten working days after notice to do so, make a written report to the chief of police or fire chief, setting forth in writing the cause of such false alarm, the corrective action taken, whether the alarm system has been inspected by an authorized service person, and such other information as the chief of police may reasonably require to determine the cause of such false alarm and corrective action necessary.
b. Each and every false alarm over two which requires a response to a premises, during any calendar year period, where there have already occurred two responses during the same period, shall be deemed to constitute a misdemeanor violation and the violator shall be punished by a minimum fine of $100.00.
c. False alarm violation number four within a calendar year period shall be deemed to constitute a misdemeanor violation hereof and shall be punishable by a minimum fine of $200.00. False alarm violation number five within a calendar year period shall be deemed to constitute a misdemeanor violation hereof and shall be punishable by a minimum fine of $400.00. Any additional false alarm violations over five within a calendar year period shall be deemed to constitute a misdemeanor violation hereof and shall be punishable by a minimum fine of $800.00.
(2) Use of a non-registered alarm system by any person is unlawful and shall constitute a misdemeanor violation and shall be punishable by a minimum fine of $100.00.
(3) Within 15 working days after a false alarm violation has been committed, the police department shall notify the property owner that the false alarm violation has occurred and the steps necessary to answer the charge.

749: The purpose of the rules and regulations contained in this chapter is to provide for the protection of the public health by prescribing the manner of storage, collection, transportation, and disposal of residential and industrial waste, rubbish, garbage, and refuse.
750:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Collector means a person, or business, who, under agreements, verbal or written, with or without compensation, does the work of collecting and/or transporting solid waste from industries, offices, retail outlets, businesses, institutions, or similar locations, and/or from residential dwellings; provided, however, that this definition shall not include an individual collecting or transporting waste from the individual's own single-family dwelling unit.
Construction and demolition waste means a type of solid waste consisting of waste building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair and demolition operations on pavement, houses, commercial buildings and other structures. Construction and demolition debris includes trees, stumps, and brush removed from property during construction, maintenance or repair of structures.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where any treatment, utilization, processing, or disposition of solid waste occurs.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal, including administration, personnel, land, equipment, design, and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Disposal site means the location or land area where the final disposition of solid waste occurs.
Garbage means putrescible animal and vegetable wastes resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking, and consumption of food.
Hazardous waste means solid or liquid waste material resulting from the manufacture or use of pesticides and drugs, other than normal household use; pathological wastes; highly flammable or explosive wastes; toxic wastes; sewage sludge; and other waste material determined to be a likely hazard to the public health, safety, or environment, except radioactive waste materials as provided for in Rules of the Department of Human Resources, chapter 270-5-20, entitled "Radioactive Materials." Hazardous wastes are prohibited in the city.
Industrial waste means waste materials generated in industrial operations. Such wastes are prohibited in the city unless the operator/owner disposes of such outside the city in compliance with all applicable regulations.
Open dump means a disposal site at which solid waste from one or more sources is consolidated and left to decompose, burn, or to otherwise create environmental pollution or a nuisance. Open dumps are prohibited in the city.
Putrescible wastes means wastes that are capable of being decomposed by microorganisms, including kitchen wastes, manure, offal, hatchery and poultry wastes, and garbage. Putrescible wastes are prohibited in the city unless the operator/owner disposes of such in compliance with all applicable regulations.
Reclamation means a controlled method of sorting and storing solid wastes for future use in accordance with an approved plan. The city does not provide for such, except as to garbage and rubbish.
Refuse means all putrescible and nonputrescible solid wastes, except body wastes, including garbage, rubbish, ashes, street cleanings, dead animals, abandoned automobiles, and solid commercial and industrial wastes. The city does not collect or contract for the collection of such, except garbage and rubbish.
Rubbish means nonputrescible solid wastes, excluding ashes, consisting of both combustible and noncombustible wastes, such as paper, cardboard, tin cans, yard clippings, wood, glass, bedding, crockery, and similar materials.
Sanitary landfilling means a method of disposing of putrescible waste or hazardous waste on land by placing an earth cover thereon. Sanitary landfills are prohibited in the city, as it has no sites suitable for such.
Scavenge means uncontrolled picking from discarded waste materials. Scavenging is prohibited in the city.
Solid waste means putrescible and nonputrescible wastes, except water-carried body wastes, including garbage, rubbish, ashes, street refuse, dead animals, sewage sludge, animal manures, industrial wastes, residue from incineration, food processing wastes, construction wastes, hazardous wastes, byproducts, waste and remains from agricultural processes including poultry processing, and any other waste material in a solid or semisolid state not otherwise defined in this chapter. Solid wastes (except garbage and rubbish) are prohibited in the city unless the operator/owner disposes of such in compliance with all applicable regulations.
Solid waste handling means the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposing of solid wastes, or any combination thereof.
Transfer station means a facility used to transfer solid wastes from one transportation vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal facility. Transfer stations are not currently allowed in the city, as it has no areas zoned for such and are not desirable.
751:
(a) Administrative responsibilities. The manager or a designated representative shall:
(1) Be responsible for the administration and enforcement of this chapter and such other responsibilities for contracting out the collection of solid waste;
(2) Inspect and regulate the operations of private collectors and private transportation and disposal systems to ensure that such operations are in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
(b) Limitations of authority. All regulatory actions shall be subject to the full review of the mayor and council.
(c) Appeal. Any person aggrieved by a requirement of this chapter, or a fee charged for the collection of waste from the person's premises, shall have the right to appeal to the mayor and council, which body may, upon hearing, confirm, modify, or revoke such requirement or fee.
752: Any person convicted of violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be punished in accordance with section 1-7. As an alternative, any residence or business that receives more than three documented notices, either verbally or written, of receptacles left at curbside longer than prescribed in section 30-25(c), shall be subject to have their collection suspended. Reinstatement shall be at the reasonable judgment of the code enforcement officer, considering the seriousness of the offense, and upon written commitment of the violator to comply in the future.
755:
(a) Generally. No person shall keep or store garbage and/or rubbish outside of any residence or building within the city, except in proper containers for collection or otherwise prepared as set forth in this section or under the express prior approval of the manager or a designated agent. Any unauthorized accumulation of garbage and/or rubbish is hereby declared to be a nuisance and is prohibited. Any storage or placement of solid waste (other than temporary small quantities of garbage and rubbish in approved trash cans for pickup) is prohibited. Upon complaint by a citizen, or on the manager's own initiative, the manager, or a designee, by written notice, shall notify the violator to remove the accumulation. Failure to remove after such written notice shall be deemed a violation of this article and subject to penalties set forth in section 30-4. A separate violation shall be deemed committed each day during or upon which such unlawful accumulation continues.
(b) Containers.
(1) Generally. Garbage containers shall be provided by the owner or occupant of each residence, business or institution sufficient in number to accommodate such waste generated by the residence or establishment between collections. Containers shall be of durable metal or plastic and shall be watertight, nonabsorbent, rust-resistant, rodent-proof, and easily cleanable. They shall be equipped with handles and tightly fitted covers and shall have a capacity of not less than 15 gallons nor more than 32 gallons, except that bulk containers of a type suitable for collection with mechanical equipment may be used. Commercial businesses and institutions may use dumpsters to comply with subsection (b)(3) of this section. Containers failing to comply with this section that have defects causing them to scatter waste upon the ground during collection or causing them to hamper or to injure the persons collecting waste shall be promptly replaced. All trash in containers shall be bagged and tied.
(2) Garbage container screening. Commercial businesses and institutions with garbage containers shall place the containers behind their building or have disposal areas that are screened from view by placement of a solid wood fence or masonry wall from five to eight feet in height. All refuse materials shall be contained within the refuse area and in acceptable containers described in subsection (b)(1) of this section. Storage area for residential properties shall be the rear of the home or screened from view from the street or roadway.
(3) Dumpster maintenance.
a. Owners, occupants and, when appropriate, service providers are responsible for keeping dumpsters in a serviceable condition. The area surrounding dumpsters shall be free and clear of any accumulations of refuse. All refuse shall be properly deposited in the container in a manner to prevent scatter. Where two or more occupants share the same dumpster, it shall be the joint responsibility of all of the users to maintain the surroundings of the dumpster.
b. All dumpsters shall have lids to prevent scatter by wind, birds or by creating vermin infestation.
c. Rusted, damaged or unsightly dumpsters shall be replaced by the service provider.
d. All dumpsters shall be emptied on a schedule to prevent overflow of refuse to surrounding areas.
e. Use of roll-off type dumpsters shall be limited to the uses as defined in section 30-2 under the term "construction and demolition waste." Any other use is prohibited.
f. Dumpsters located at food service establishments shall comply with environmental health service regulations.
(c) Placement. On days designated as collection days for the respective routes by the contracting agency, garbage and/or rubbish shall be placed for collection no further than five feet from the curb or roadside front of the residence or establishment owning the garbage or rubbish, or if the property abuts on an alley, at the rear of the property, but not in the gutter or in the street or alley in such manner as to interfere with pedestrian or vehicular traffic. All containers shall be placed before 7:00 a.m. on the day of collection or the night prior to collection and returned to their storage area by 7:00 p.m. the next day.
(d) Scavenging. No person other than the owner or authorized collection personnel shall sift the contents of or remove anything from containers, boxes, or bundles containing garbage or rubbish.
756:
(a) Frequency. Garbage and rubbish shall be collected from residential premises once a week. No person or entity shall engage in the collection of any garbage and/or rubbish or recyclable materials from dumpsters, containers, or receptacles of any kind or type except during the hours of 7:00 a.m. until 9:00 p.m. unless performing emergency work to safeguard the immediate health, safety and welfare of the public.
(b) Limitations. Industrial waste, dead animals, waste from construction, demolition, landscaping, or processing operations, and any other waste besides garbage and rubbish will not be collected, transported, or disposed of by public facilities. Such waste collection, transportation, and disposal shall be by the owners or generators of such waste or animals.
(c) Collection vehicles. Vehicles used for collection and transportation of garbage and rubbish shall be kept clean and in good repair. They shall be constructed in such manner that the contents thereof cannot be spilled, leaked, or blown from the vehicle. They shall be readily identifiable by letters, not less than three inches high and easily legible, painted on the door of the vehicle cab or in an equally conspicuous place, showing the owner's name, telephone number, state permit number, truck number, and rated load capacity in cubic yards.
(d) Private contractors. No person other than employees of the city and contractors with the city shall collect, transport, or dispose of solid waste for pay in the city without having first applied for and received a license to engage in such business as provided in chapter 34, article II. Privately contracted collectors engaged in providing collection services shall:
(1) Comply with local, state and federal rules and regulations regarding the storage, handling, transporting and disposing of garbage and rubbish and other materials.
(2) Dispose of garbage and rubbish only at landfills permitted by the environmental protection division (EPD) of the state department of natural resources when disposing within the state. The transfer of any refuse into receptacles serviced, or onto property within the city is prohibited.
(3) Operate only approved garbage and rubbish transportation vehicles designed or modified to prevent debris from dropping or blowing away, and sealed to prevent waste liquids from spilling on the streets.
(4) Obtain any other permits required by law.
(e) Construction/demolition contractors.
(1) The property owner and the prime contractor in charge of a construction site and/or demolition site shall be required to furnish containers for materials produced by construction and by workers. All materials from construction, demolition or related activities shall be picked up and placed in containers by the end of each workday. Provided, however, that construction material and debris which cannot be blown away by wind or blown or carried away by any other natural force shall not be affected by this provision until completion of said construction or demolition.
(2) The location of bulk containers used at construction/demolition sites shall meet the approval of the code enforcement officer or building inspector.
757: All disposal of garbage and rubbish shall be at the contractor's disposal sites operated in accordance with state laws and with rules and regulations of the state department of natural resources, and at no other place. The establishment of any private waste disposal facility, agricultural byproducts recycling facility, or other solid waste, garbage, or similar facility must be approved by the city, such approval to be based upon applicable regulations.
760:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Commercial solid waste means all types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses and other nonmanufacturing activities, excluding residential and industrial wastes.
Composting means the controlled biological decomposition of organic matter into a stable, odor-free humus.
Leachate collection system means a system at a landfill for collection of the leachate which may percolate through the waste and into the soils surrounding the landfill.
Municipal solid waste means any solid waste derived from households, including garbage, trash and sanitary waste in septic tanks and includes solid waste from single-family and multifamily residences, hotels and motels, bunkhouses, campgrounds, picnic grounds, and day use recreation areas. The term "municipal solid waste" includes yard trimmings and commercial solid waste but does not include solid waste from mining, agricultural or sylvicultural operations or industrial processes or operations.
Municipal solid waste disposal facility means any facility or location where the final deposition of any amount of municipal solid waste occurs, whether or not mixed with or including commercial or industrial solid waste, including, but not limited to, municipal solid waste landfills.
Municipal solid waste landfill means a disposal facility where any amount of municipal solid waste, whether or not mixed with or including commercial waste, industrial waste, nonhazardous sludges or small quantity generator hazardous waste, is disposed of by means of placing an approved cover thereon.
Yard trimmings means leaves, brush, grass clippings, shrub and tree prunings, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals, and vegetative matter resulting from landscaping development and maintenance, other than mining, agricultural and silvicultural operations.

(a) Maintenance and repair of public streets. All maintenance and repair of public streets, alleys, curbs, sidewalks, and other public ways shall be under the supervision of the mayor or a designee.
(b) Maintenance of sidewalks. It shall be the duty of all owners of property in the city upon which sidewalks have been laid to keep such walkways in good repair at all times.
(c) Maintenance of property between sidewalks and street. All persons who own real estate in the city which abuts upon any sidewalk which is paved shall be required to keep that portion of such sidewalk which lies between the property line and curbline of the adjoining street, and upon which the owner's real estate abuts, in good and smooth condition and free from growing weeds and other obnoxious and unsightly vegetation or other things which would mar or detract from the beauty and cleanliness of the street upon which their property abuts. Any property owner who shall place or allow grass to grow upon the portion of the sidewalk lying between the property line and curbline of the street, and upon which the owner's real estate abuts, shall keep such grass properly mowed and free from rubbish of all kinds. If such owners are not in the possession of their property, then this section shall apply to their tenants or those who have possession or control of the property.
(d) Defacing sidewalks, streets, and curbs. It shall be unlawful for any person to deface any public sidewalk, street, or curb in the city by painting any signs thereon, whether for commercial advertising purposes or not, or to walk or drive any vehicle upon or injure in any way any newly laid street, sidewalk, or curbing pavement while the same is guarded by a warning sign or barricade or is soft or newly laid.
(e) Obstructions. It shall be unlawful for any person to cause, create, or maintain any obstruction on any street, alley, sidewalk, or other public way, except as may be provided in this chapter or other ordinances and laws of the city.
(f) Deposits and discharges into streets and sidewalks.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit on any street or sidewalk any material which may be harmful to the pavement thereof, or any waste material, or any glass or other article which may do injury to any person, animal, or property.
(2) It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge or allow to be discharged onto any public street or sidewalk any water or other fluid material containing objectionable material such as sewage, waste, milk, or other organic material.
(g) Private use. It shall be unlawful for any person to use any street, sidewalk, or other public place as space for the display of goods or merchandise without first obtaining a sidewalk display permit on a form prescribed by the manager; or to write or make any sign or advertisement on any such pavement.
(h) Encroachments. It shall be unlawful for any person to erect or maintain any building or structure which encroaches upon any public street or property, or to erect any poles or wires or maintain any poles or wires over any public place, street, alley, or other public way, without having first secured a permit from the city clerk in the manner specified in this chapter.
(i) Openings. It shall be unlawful for any person to construct or maintain any opening or stairway in any public street, sidewalk, or alley without first obtaining a permit from the city clerk in the manner specified in this chapter.
(j) Trees and shrubs.
(1) Planting and removal. It shall be unlawful for any person to plant, remove, injure, or cut any tree, bush, or shrub in or from any public street, parkway, or other public place without first obtaining permission therefor from the city clerk in the manner specified in this chapter.
(2) Advertisements. It shall be unlawful for any person to attach any sign, advertisement, or notice to any tree or shrub in any public place.
(3) Dangerous trees. Any tree or shrub which overhangs any sidewalk, street, or other public place in the city in such a way as to impede or interfere with traffic or travel shall be trimmed by the owner of the premises on which such tree or shrub grows so that the obstruction shall cease.
(4) Poles and wires. Any person or company which maintains poles and wires in the streets, alleys or other public places in the city shall keep such wires and poles free and away from any nearby trees or shrubs properly trimmed, subject to the direction of the public works supervisor, so that no injury shall befall either the poles and wires or the shrubs and trees by their contact.
(k) Burning of leaves and rubbish. It shall be unlawful for any person to burn any leaves, paper, rubbish, or other substances upon any of the public streets, sidewalks, or alleys of the city.
(Code 1982, § 22-101; Code 1994, § 34-2; Ord. of 9-20-2023)

(2) Satisfactory to the city attorney in form and substance; and
(3) Conditioned upon the permittee's agreement to secure and hold harmless the city and its officers arising from the excavation and other work covered by the excavation permit or for which the city, the city council, or any city officer may be made liable by reason of any accident or injury to persons or property guarding the excavation or for any other injury resulting from the negligence of the permittee, and further conditioned on the permittee's agreement to fill up, restore, and place in good and safe condition as near as may be to its original condition, and to the satisfaction of the supervisor of streets, all openings and excavations made in streets, and to maintain any street where excavation is made in as good condition for the period of 24 months after the work shall have been done, usual wear and tear excepted, as it was in before the work shall have been done. 780:

817:
(a) Requests to use public property. Groups have from time to time sought to use public property and roads in the city. The city has reviewed the adverse impact events have on city services and residents.
(b) Private uses of public property should not interfere with safety. It is in the public interest that the uses described not interfere with the rights of citizens not participating, nor endanger public safety, nor obstruct orderly flow of traffic. Thus it is proper for security, welfare, health and safety of citizens and for preservation of peace and order that rules be established. The Supreme Court held that government, to regulate competing uses of public forums, may impose a permit requirement on those wishing to hold a march, parade, or rally, and such must meet requirements. It may not delegate overly broad licensing discretion to a government official nor be based on the message. It must be narrowly tailored to serve a significant government interest and leave open ample alternatives for communication. The standards for the fee must use narrowly drawn, reasonable and definite standards.

(a) Manager. The manager shall be the administrator for receipt and processing of applications for a permit for a parade, demonstration, march, rally, assembly, TV, movie or ad filming, road closing, or other use of public property and roads.
(b) Organization or group. This shall apply to any entity or group of more than five individuals or their representatives.
(c) Private purpose event. Private purpose event shall be any purpose (not commanded or directed by statute, ordinance or other regulation to be performed by the government) such as parade, demonstration, march, assembly, picket line, rally or gathering for a common purpose, TV, movie, or ad filming, road closing, or similar, that has a tendency to interfere with normal pedestrian or vehicular traffic or that occupies a public area in a place open to the public. Funerals, school supervised activities, and recreational facilities for recreational purposes are excluded from this definition.

(a) Permit required. Every organization or group who wishes to use public property or roads for a private purpose event must have a permit from the city, unless such permit is prohibited under law or the activity is exempted by law.
(b) Application required. Every organization or group required to procure a permit shall submit an application to the manager, which shall conform to the requirements of this section and all other applicable laws.
(c) Timeliness. Each application shall be on forms prescribed by the manager and submitted no less than 30 days prior to the activity, for security checks, verifications and arrangements to be made. The scheduling shall be first come, first served, based on date application received. The city does not hold dates without a complete application. The manager will act within 30 days of receipt of complete application.
(d) Information. Each application shall contain the following plus the information on the application form:
(1) Name and home address of applicant if an individual, or main office address if an entity or other organization, and phone number;
(2) Date, time and place of the activity, including proposed routes;
(3) Kind and class of activity to be carried on;
(4) Name and addresses of the partners, officers, directors and/or members; and
(5) Record of all convictions of every partner, officer, member or director for violation of any laws or ordinance of any government, not minor traffic violations.
(e) Complete and signed. The application must be complete with all required documents/attachments and submitted 30 days prior to start date. Incomplete applications submitted after the 30 day deadline will be denied. Each application shall be signed and sworn to by applicant if an individual, or by a partner, director or officer.
(f) Administrative purposes. All information under the authority of this section should be used solely in administering the provisions of this section.
(g) False statements. False statements in any application shall be grounds for immediate revocation, denial, and/or denial of future applications.
(h) Fees. Fees shall be in the amount established by resolution and accompany the application.
(i) Toilets. Events require restrooms that are both ADA accessible and non-accessible, in the immediate area of the event site which will be available to the public. One restroom for each 500 persons plus one ADA restroom for each 1,500 persons.
(j) Sidewalks. No vehicles can be placed, parked, driven over or staged on a sidewalk. No dumpsters, tents, chairs, benches, trash cans, or other temporary structures or items can be on a sidewalk or streets without a compelling showing of need and showing the plans for such, and formal written approval from the city.

(1) Prepare and provide for the forms for application for a permit and submission of any information necessary to properly administer and enforce this article;

(3) Issue a permit within ten days of approval. However, when objectively deemed appropriate for the public health, safety and welfare, the application may be referred to council to be publicly discussed and decided by mayor and council.

Otherwise, unless some material interference with the rights of nonparticipant citizens exists, or orderly flow of traffic would be obstructed unreasonably, or there is a reasonable likelihood of a clear and present danger to citizens, or there would be other unreasonable interference with the welfare, peace, safety, health, good order and convenience of the public, the permit shall be granted.

The occupation tax only applies to those businesses and occupations which are covered by the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-5 to 48-13-26. All other applicable businesses and occupations are taxed by the local government pursuant to the pertinent general and/or local law and ordinance.
(Code 1994, § 10-60; Ord. of 9-14-1994, § 10-70)
851:
(a) Each such occupation tax shall be for the calendar year 1995 and succeeding calendar years thereafter unless otherwise specifically provided. Such registration and occupation tax shall be payable on or after January 1 of each year and shall, if not paid by March 15 of each year, be subject to penalties for delinquency as prescribed in this article. On any new profession, trade or calling begun in the city after March 15, 1995, or after March 15 of any succeeding year thereafter, the registration and tax shall be delinquent if not obtained immediately upon beginning business. The tax registration provided for in this article shall be issued by the city clerk and if any person whose duty it is to obtain a registration shall, after registration or occupation tax becomes delinquent, transact or offer to transact in the city any of the kind of profession, trade or calling subject to this article without having first obtained such registration, such offender shall, upon conviction by the municipal court, be punished by a fine not to exceed $500.00 for each day such violation continues.
(b) At the time of payment of the tax provided for in this article, each person liable for such tax shall make a sworn statement as to the number of persons employed by the taxpayer, or as to the election of the appropriate tax upon professionals described in this article.
(c) In addition to the remedies listed in subsections (a) and (b) of this section, the city may proceed to collect in the same manner as provided by law for tax executions.
(Code 1994, §§ 10-61, 10-70; Ord. of 9-14-1994, §§ 10-71, 10-80)

852:

861:
In addition to any other remedies provided in this article for the collection of the occupation tax levied in this article, the city, upon any tax or installment of such tax becoming delinquent and remaining unpaid, shall issue execution for the correct amount of the tax against the persons liable for the tax, which execution shall bear interest at the rate of 12 percent per annum from the date when such tax or installment becomes delinquent, and the lien shall cover the property of the person liable for the tax, all as provided by the ordinances and the city Charter and the laws of the state. The lien of the occupation tax shall become fixed on, and date from, the date such tax or any installment thereof became delinquent. The execution shall be levied by the city marshal, or other officer duly authorized by the city, upon the property of the defendant located in the jurisdiction, and sufficient property shall be advertised and sold to pay the amount of the execution, with interest and costs. All other proceedings in relation thereto shall be had as is provided by ordinances and the city Charter and the laws of the state, and the defendant in the execution shall have rights of defense, by affidavit of illegality and otherwise, which are provided by the applicable laws in regard to tax executions. When a nulla bona entry has been entered by proper authority upon an execution issued by the city against any person defaulting on the occupation tax, the person against whom the entry was made shall not be allowed or entitled to have or collect any fees or charges whatsoever for services rendered after the entry of the nulla bona. If, at any time after the entry of nulla bona has been made, the person against whom the execution issues pays the tax, in full, together with all interest and costs accrued on the tax, the person may collect any fees and charges due such person as though such person had never defaulted in the payment of the taxes.
